lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: The Velvet Collapse, one sixteen point five. Funk, at the edge of a dying star. Mind the window.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: You're in the Velvet Lounge, Casino Ultima. The star outside is enormous, and not long for this world. Enjoy them both.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: The Baron, on the Velvet Collapse. The groove is mine. The star is somebody else's problem.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: The Velvet Collapse. It's late, the star is swelling, and the dress code is fireproof velvet.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: The Velvet Collapse. Daytime, they tell me. Out here we only have two times. Before four, and after.

lines.speaker: Odette, the Croupier
lines.text: Casino Ultima. The house always wins.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: And the star always comes back. The Velvet Collapse.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: That's Old Ruby out there, filling the window. A red giant, three hundred times wider than she used to be. Aren't we all, darling.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: She's dying, of course. She's been dying for years. She makes it look absolutely wonderful.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: People ask me, Baron, aren't you worried about the supernova? Worried? It's the finest lighting rig in the galaxy, and I don't pay a penny for it.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Every night at four, the whole room goes white, and the band looks incredible. You can't buy that. Believe me. I've asked.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Our roulette wheel has only red on it. Thirty seven pockets, all red. We had a black one once. It was lost in the year of the big flare, and we never replaced it.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Nobody's complained. Everybody wins, a little. That's not how a casino works, but then, very little out here is.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: A word about insurance. Casino Ultima is fully insured against the star exploding. Our insurers have paid out every single night for eleven years.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: They've been very gracious about it. They send a card. This year's card just says, again?

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: The house band tonight, as every night, is the Late Expansion. On drums, Ignatius Bell. On keys, the lovely Delphine Starr.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: And on bass guitar, me. I'm wonderful. Don't tell me. I know.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Hello, love. It's Bev. Is this the request line?

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Bev, darling, there's no request line at the edge of a dying star. There's just this line, and it's yours. What'll it be?

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Something slow, please.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Bev. Nothing here is slow. But I'll see what I can do.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Good evening. The doors of Casino Ultima are open, the velvet's been brushed, and Ruby is looking especially red tonight.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Radiant, really. Don't tell her. She's sensitive about her size.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: A relay ship has drifted into our orbit tonight. Lights low, very polite. Welcome to the outer reaches, newcomer.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: A word of advice. Don't sit too near the window at four. And do tip the croupier. She remembers.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Tonight's collapse comes to you courtesy of Grumbel's Ladders. From the top of a Grumbel's ladder, a supernova is just a very bright evening.

lines.speaker: Arnold Grumbel
lines.text: Grumbel's Ladders. Up is a choice.

lines.speaker: Odette, the Croupier
lines.text: Place your bets, ladies and gentlemen. Place your bets.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Let's see how the tables are doing. Odette?

lines.speaker: Odette, the Croupier
lines.text: Bets are open, Baron.

lines.speaker: Odette, the Croupier
lines.text: The gentleman in the silver jacket bets that tonight, the star won't go. He has placed that bet every night for eleven years. He has lost every night for eleven years.

lines.speaker: Odette, the Croupier
lines.text: He says the night he wins, he'll be the richest man in the galaxy. For about four seconds.

lines.speaker: Odette, the Croupier
lines.text: Table four would like to bet on the colour of the flash. White, very white, or blinding.

lines.speaker: Odette, the Croupier
lines.text: The house recommends blinding.

lines.speaker: Odette, the Croupier
lines.text: A lady at the bar bets her coat that she can finish her drink before four o'clock. Her coat is velvet. Her drink is very large.

lines.speaker: Odette, the Croupier
lines.text: The room is quietly on her side.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Somebody has bet the house that the star comes back tomorrow.

lines.speaker: Odette, the Croupier
lines.text: Accepted.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: It always comes back. We stopped taking that bet years ago. We take it anyway. It's tradition.

lines.speaker: Odette, the Croupier
lines.text: A first-time guest bets everything that he'll see the dawn. Sir. There is no dawn. There's a supernova, and then breakfast.

lines.speaker: Odette, the Croupier
lines.text: He has changed his bet to breakfast.

lines.speaker: Odette, the Croupier
lines.text: A reminder that our chips are made of cooled starlight. Please don't put them in your mouth.

lines.speaker: Odette, the Croupier
lines.text: They are much warmer than they look. So, frankly, is the starlight.

lines.speaker: Odette, the Croupier
lines.text: No more bets.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Nobody ever listens to her. Here's the band.

lines.speaker: Odette, the Croupier
lines.text: The wheel is spinning.

lines.speaker: Odette, the Croupier
lines.text: Red. It's always red.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Good evening, and welcome to the Velvet Hour. Coats in the cloakroom, sunglasses in the pocket, and the star in the window. For now.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: The kitchen tonight recommends the flambé. Everything in here is flambé after four o'clock, so the chef likes to get in early.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Here's something to eat by. Slowly, darling. There's time. Not much. But some.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Dance with whoever you came with. Or don't. At four o'clock we all leave together anyway, at the speed of light, and come back for breakfast.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: It's terribly romantic, if you don't think about it too hard. I never do.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: It's three o'clock at the Velvet Collapse. One hour to collapse. Ladies and gentlemen, the Final Hour.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: The window has gone from red to a sort of very loud red. That's quite normal. Ruby's taking a deep breath.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Order your last drinks now, please. Somewhere around four, the bar will be briefly made of light.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: The staff are coming round with the sunglasses. Please take a pair, and put them on when the band does.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: The band put theirs on eleven years ago, and have never taken them off. They say it's for the supernova. I have my doubts.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Did you feel that? That's Ruby. She does this towards the end. A little shiver, right through the floor.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: The roulette ball has jumped into red. Well. It was always going to be red.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Odette, I think it's time.

lines.speaker: Odette, the Croupier
lines.text: Ladies and gentlemen, the house is no longer taking bets on the end of the world. It's too close to call.

lines.speaker: Odette, the Croupier
lines.text: We are, however, taking bets on breakfast.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: The band always plays a little faster in the Final Hour. They're trying to fit in one more chorus before the end.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Eleven years, they've never managed it. Tonight, I think they might. Listen to them go.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Ladies and gentlemen, it's four o'clock. Sunglasses on, please.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Five. Four. Three. Two. One.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Lovely.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: We're in the white now. The room is very bright and very quiet and a little warm, like the inside of a lamp. Don't be alarmed.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: The band's still playing. You just can't see them. You can hear me, which is the main thing.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Right. Is everybody still here? Silver jacket? Yes. The lady with the very large drink? Finished it. Well done. Odette?

lines.speaker: Odette, the Croupier
lines.text: Present.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Good. Nobody ever goes anywhere. We just get very, very bright for a while.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Housekeeping are sweeping the stardust off the dance floor. It all goes in a little velvet bag, and the bags go in the gift shop.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Supernova dust. One careful owner. Lightly exploded.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Good morning from the Velvet Collapse. You'll be pleased to hear the star is fine. Ruby pulled herself back together at about half past five, the way she does.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: She's looking a little embarrassed. Nobody mention it.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Breakfast is served in the lounge. Eggs, toast, coffee, and a view of a red giant who exploded last night and is now acting as if nothing happened.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Honestly, darling. We've all been there.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Ultima Fireproof Velvet. The jacket that doesn't mind the end of the world.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: I've been wearing mine for eleven years. Eleven supernovas. Not a scorch on it. The lapels have never looked better.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Ultima Fireproof Velvet. Rated to one supernova per night. Dry clean only.

clips.title: In the Event of a Supernova

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: A message from the management of Casino Ultima.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: In the event of a supernova, please remain in your seat, keep your sunglasses on, and hold your drink level. Do not run. There is nowhere to run to, and the carpet is new.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: And please, do not tip the star. The star is not staff.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: I listened to the Quiet Corner last night, on the Lounge at the End of Time. Greg's show. I turned the speaker up so far the star started listening.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Not a sound. Marvellous. The man's a minimalist. Four stars. Ruby gives it five.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Somebody at the bar says a moon has gone missing. Not ours, darling. We haven't had a moon since Ruby swallowed it. She does that.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Check under the roulette table, just in case.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Does the whole lounge smell of toast, or is it me? We do smell of toast after four, usually. It's early for toast. Odette?

lines.speaker: Odette, the Croupier
lines.text: It isn't the star, Baron.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Then somebody, somewhere, is making breakfast.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: The band has started playing a song nobody wrote. Everybody knows it. Now they've stopped, right before the end, and they're looking at me.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: I don't know how it ends either, darlings. Play it again.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Three knocks on the stage door. Odette opened it. Nothing out there but a red giant and a very long way down.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Close it, darling. Whoever it is, they're welcome. They'll need sunglasses.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: The star has gone a colour. Not red. Not white. A colour I have never seen in eleven years of watching her explode.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: Odette, put it on the wheel. We'll call it Ruby's Own.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: A pigeon has just walked into the Velvet Lounge. No ship, no ladder. It walked past the doorman like they were old friends.

lines.speaker: Baron Velour
lines.text: It's at the bar now. It's having what I'm having. I like it.
